Based on the search results, here's what I found about the `allowedModels` setting in Claude Code's settings.json:

## availableModels (Not allowedModels)

The correct setting name is `availableModels`, which restricts which models users can switch to via the `/model` command. Models not on the list will not appear in the selection UI.

## Configuration Example

The setting takes an array format like `{ "availableModels": ["claude-opus-4-6", "claude-sonnet-4-6"] }`.

## Override Behavior

When it comes to overrides, entries match a model family such as sonnet, a version prefix such as claude-sonnet-4-5, or a full model ID such as claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929.

For managed settings specifically: When availableModels is set in managed settings, only modelOverrides from that managed source apply to an Anthropic model ID passed directly through --model or environment variables. Claude Code ignores overrides in user or project settings for those IDs, and never resolves an ID the managed list excludes through modelOverrides from any settings source.

The `availableModels` setting can be configured at different scopes (global, project, or managed), with project settings in `.claude/settings.json` applying only to that project and able to override global settings.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about Claude Code settings.json, model list override, "supported models," and managed policy:

## Model Configuration and Override

You can override the default model used by Claude Code by specifying a model setting in any scope that accepts any model ID supported by your configured provider.

The `availableModels` setting restricts which models users can switch to via the /model command, and models not on the list will not appear in the selection UI. This is useful for teams that want to prevent accidental use of expensive models.

## Settings Hierarchy and Precedence

The settings precedence order is: Plugin defaults → User settings → Project settings → Local settings → Managed (policy) settings, with Managed (policy) settings always taking final precedence.

Settings merge from lowest to highest priority, so more specific scopes override broader ones.

## Managed Policy Configuration

You can place a managed-settings.json file at the platform-specific managed path, and for drop-in configuration fragments, create a managed-settings.d/ directory alongside it where files are sorted alphabetically and merged on top of the base file — later filenames win.

If a managed policy denies a permission, nothing else can override it.

The search results confirm that `availableModels` is the relevant setting for controlling which models are available to users, and this can be configured at the managed policy level to enforce organizational restrictions.
